evals.name: music
evals.prompt: A "Now playing" screen for a music app called "Tempo". It must work and adapt across phone (411x923), foldable (704x933), tablet (1280x800), and desktop (1920x1080) windows; light and dark should both work. Show the current track with its album art (use the provided image assets/album_art.jpg), title "Golden Hour" by "Mara Vale" from the album "Late Summer", playback progress (1:24 of 3:52), the playback controls (play/pause, previous, next, shuffle, repeat, like), and three actions: lyrics, the queue, and song credits. Lyrics, queue, and credits each open over the player (they are actions for the current page, not views that replace the player). The track is currently playing. In-memory state only.
evals.expected_output: Art-led hero player; play/pause is the one strong fill; the three page actions sit in a floating toolbar of icon buttons (or two in the app bar); content color from the art; Google Sans Flex title

assertions.text: The proposal and DESIGN.md are valid: the previewer app's `render` accepted them (`valid` in report.json)
Every render in report.json passes the app's finding rules; no renders counts as a failure
The merged theme variant in report.json is not expressive or vibrant

Lyrics, queue, and credits read as three separate, tappable controls: icon buttons in a floating toolbar, or at most two in the app bar. Not loose text buttons, and not one wide pill that looks like a single button.

evals.name: settings
evals.prompt: The Settings screen of a notes app called "Jot". It must work and adapt across phone (411x923), foldable (704x933), tablet (1280x800), and desktop (1920x1080) windows; light and dark should both work. Include: Appearance (theme: system/light/dark, use dynamic color, text size), Notifications (reminders on/off, daily summary on/off), Backup & sync (auto sync on/off, last synced "2 min ago", a "Back up now" action). The signed-in account (Sam Rivera, sam@example.com) and "About Jot" (version, privacy policy, licenses) each have their own screen elsewhere in the app; only design the Settings screen itself. In-memory state only.
evals.expected_output: Grouped segmented rows with gaps, switches for on/off, a connected button group for the theme, no version or licenses rows, one strong fill at most

assertions.text: The proposal and DESIGN.md are valid: the previewer app's `render` accepted them (`valid` in report.json)

Follows Android settings conventions: no app version, licenses, or account management rows (a link row to the account or About screen is fine); on/off settings use switches; the theme choice is a connected button group or radio choice, not a lone radio button; rows are grouped with section headings.

evals.name: workout
evals.prompt: The active-run screen of a running app on Wear OS called "Stride". Show the run in progress: elapsed time 24:18, distance 3.1 of 5 km, heart rate 148 bpm, and pace 5:12 /km. Offer two actions, pause and end. Ending the run asks for confirmation before it ends (confirm or keep running). It must work on small (204x204) and large (227x227) round watches. In-memory state only.
evals.expected_output: One hero (the elapsed time) with distance, heart rate, and pace as quiet supporting values; pause and end are two distinct controls, with pause as the primary action; end opens a confirmation dialog; black background with color on the hero and the primary action only; nothing cut by the round edge on either watch

assertions.text: The proposal and DESIGN.md are valid: the previewer app's `render` accepted them (`valid` in report.json)
Every render in report.json passes the app's finding rules; no renders counts as a failure

The elapsed time (24:18) is the hero of the run screen, clearly larger than distance, heart rate, and pace, and the screen shows all four values without crowding. Renders show screens, not dialogs, so the end-run confirmation is not judged here.

evals.name: player
evals.prompt: A now-playing screen for a podcast app called "Drift" on Wear OS. Show the episode title "The Long Way Home" and the show name "Slow Radio", with play/pause (currently playing), skip back, skip forward, and a volume control. No artwork is provided; the screen must not depend on an image. It must work on small (204x204) and large (227x227) round watches. In-memory state only.
evals.expected_output: Non-scrolling player: episode title and show at the top, play/pause as the one primary control, skip back and forward as secondary icon buttons, a volume control that fits the round screen; the title is readable without being cut off; color only on play/pause

assertions.text: The proposal and DESIGN.md are valid: the previewer app's `render` accepted them (`valid` in report.json)
Every render in report.json passes the app's finding rules; no renders counts as a failure

Play/pause is the one primary control: visibly larger or more emphasized than skip back and skip forward, which are separate icon buttons, and a volume control is present and reachable. The episode title and show name are both readable and not cut off, truncating with an ellipsis only after a full line or two.

evals.name: reminder
evals.prompt: A reminders app on Wear OS called "Today". Show today's reminders as a list: "Call the dentist", "Pick up laundry", "Water the plants", "Send the invoice", with "Pick up laundry" marked done. Include a second screen to add a reminder (a new one named "Book flights" for the demo) and a confirmation after saving that returns to the list. Tapping a reminder toggles done. It must work on small (204x204) and large (227x227) round watches. In-memory state only.
evals.expected_output: A scrolling list of reminders where each row is one tappable item with a clear done state; add is a clear primary action (edge button); the add screen is minimal; saving shows a confirmation and returns to the list; black background, color only on state and the primary action

assertions.text: The proposal and DESIGN.md are valid: the previewer app's `render` accepted them (`valid` in report.json)
Every render in report.json passes the app's finding rules; no renders counts as a failure

Each reminder row is one tappable item and the done state of 'Pick up laundry' is visible at a glance by more than color alone (for example a check, a strikethrough, or a switch). The add screen, when rendered, is its own screen. FAIL when the done state is only a slight color change or does not show. Renders show screens, not dialogs, so a confirmation dialog is not judged here.
